title.narrative: Humanitarian response to provide life-saving integrated health and nutrition interventions for women and children facing acute malnutrition in Borno and Yobe states

description.narrative: ltpgtSave the Children (SC) aims to reach vulnerable populations in Borno and Yobe States by maximizing coverage, accessibility, availability, and affordability of essential health and nutrition services. The project will deliver treatment for acute malnutrition through Outpatient Therapeutic Programmes (OTPs) and inpatient care at Stabilization Centres, while integrating WASH and Child Protection interventions to improve overall wellbeing. Services will prioritize gender equality and disability inclusion, ensuring that women, men, boys, girls, and persons with disabilities can access care without barriers.ltbrgtIn collaboration with the Ministry of Health, the Primary Healthcare Development Board, and the Hospital Management Board of both states, SC will operate three newly reopened OTP sites, support 16 additional OTPs through community mobilization with Community Nutrition Mobilizers, and upgrade three Stabilization Centres with five additional beds each to strengthen capacity. SC will also reinforce disease surveillance and outbreak response by providing medical supplies to three isolation/treatment centres, training five additional health workers per centre, as well as supporting average logistics cost for state-led supervision and stipends for 30 Community Health Influencers Promoters Service (CHIPS) Agents during vaccine campaign outreaches.ltbrgtThe response will target IDPs and host communities in Kaga and Jere LGAs of Borno and Gujba LGA of Yobe. Emergency Nutrition Response will focus on life-saving interventions for Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), with emphasis on gender equality and disability inclusion. Activities will include community-based screening and referrals, upgrading two Stabilization Centres with warming systems ahead of harmattan, and resuming nutrition services in three OTPs. At General Hospital Molai, services will cover outpatient consultations, basic laboratory investigations, procurement of essential medicines, and training of health workers on Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI). Twenty-four-hour inpatient care will also be provided for children with SAM and complications.ltbrgtTo strengthen prevention, SC will enhance existing mother and father peer groups as platforms for Maternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) messaging. Mothers will receive counselling on exclusive breastfeeding and complementary feeding. Children under treatment will undergo protection screening to detect abuse, neglect, unsafe care, or exclusion due to disability or gender-based vulnerabilities, with cases managed directly or referred to specialized services. Caregivers’ knowledge in psychosocial stimulation, responsive parenting, stress management, and child development will also be improved.ltbrgtThe project will integrate Gender-Based Violence (GBV) risk mitigation and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) into nutrition programming, ensuring dignity, safety, and survivor-centered care. Protection, gender equality, diversity, disability inclusion, and accountability will be mainstreamed throughout beneficiary selection and implementation. Community volunteers - including women, men, youth, and persons with disabilities—will be engaged to promote inclusivity and shared ownership. Nutrition services will be adapted to diverse needs, while gender-segregated sanitation facilities will ensure privacy and dignity.ltbrgtThrough these interventions, the project will improve nutrition outcomes while enhancing overall health, protection, and empowerment. By embedding dignity, equity, and accountability across design and delivery, SC will safeguard vulnerable groups, advance gender equality, strengthen disability inclusion, and build more resilient communities in Borno and Yobe States.ltbrgtlt/pgt
